brief.issue: a fracture missed on X-ray at an emergency department and the patient sent home as a sprain

items.title: 202000038.pdf
items.quote: We found that C was appropriately assessed and did not meet the criteria in the relevant guidelines for their injury to have been considered high-risk and requiring imaging.
items.why: This discusses a decision not to do imaging in line with emergency injury guidelines, which is relevant to a missed fracture after a sprain diagnosis.

items.title: Scaphoid_Fractures.pdf
items.quote: You will receive a telephone consultation or fracture clinic review in the next 2 weeks.
items.why: This says patients with a possible scaphoid fracture should get a telephone or fracture clinic review within the next 2 weeks after Emergency Department discharge.

items.title: Scaphoid_Fractures.pdf
items.quote: Please ensure the Emergency Department/Minor Injury Unit reception staff have your mobile and phone home numbers.
items.why: This asks Emergency Department or Minor Injury Unit staff to record phone numbers, which supports arranging follow-up after the injury.

items.title: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh – safe delivery of care inspection report: May 2023 – Healthcare Improvement Scotland
items.quote: We carried out an unannounced inspection to the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, NHS Lothian on Monday 20 to Wednesday 22 February 2023 using our safe delivery of care inspection methodology.
items.why: This is an official inspection of the same hospital, but the quoted text only states the visit dates and method, not any emergency diagnosis or X-ray findings.

items.title: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh – safe delivery of care inspection report: May 2023 – Healthcare Improvement Scotland
items.quote: As a result of serious concerns about patient safety within the emergency department identified during this inspection we wrote to NHS Lothian to formal escalate our concerns in accordance with level 1 of our escalation process in the Healthcare Improvement Scotland and Scottish Government: operating framework.
items.why: This says the regulator formally escalated serious patient safety concerns in the emergency department, which may support a complaint about unsafe emergency care.

items.why: It says X rays only show about 70-80% of scaphoid fractures, supporting that some wrist fractures are not visible on first imaging.

items.why: It covers a wrist injury where initial X-rays did not show a clear fracture, which is similar but limited to suspected scaphoid injuries.

draft.details:
On early July 2026, I fell on my outstretched hand and attended the A&E department at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh. I was X-rayed and told it was a sprain, and I was sent home. The pain did not go away, and in mid August 2026, my GP sent me back for a second X-ray, which showed a scaphoid fracture. By November 2026, the fracture has not healed, and I now need surgery. I have also missed my second-year exams and had to stop shifts at my part-time job because I cannot use my wrist. I would like an explanation of what went wrong, treatment or support to put things right, and compensation for what happened.

For reference, policyonline.nhslothian.scot (Scaphoid_Fractures.pdf) published: "You will receive a telephone consultation or fracture clinic review in the next 2 weeks."
For reference, gloshospitals.nhs.uk (Suspected Scaphoid Injury) published: "Unfortunately, X rays only show about 70-80% of scaphoid fractures."
I would be grateful if NHS Lothian would take these into account when looking at my complaint.
draft.location: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Accident & Emergency department
draft.outcome: An explanation of what went wrong, treatment or support to put things right and compensation for what happened.
